facts.text: Dunning earned its name from the Dunning family, who donated land to Cook County for the rail line and station.
The Cook County Poor Farm, later known as the Dunning Poorhouse and Insane Asylum, opened in 1851 on a 320‑acre site northwest of Chicago for the indigent.
In 1909, Illinois enacted an act making state responsibility for the insane mandatory, shifting patients from county poorhouses to state hospitals across the state.
The Dunning Branch of the Chicago Public Library opened on May 6, 2011, serving a community that grew around the former poor farm site.
In 1916, Schorsch Brothers Real Estate bought land west of Austin and south of Irving Park, naming it West Portage Park to distance it from Dunning.
